Incorporating Beige Book signals into the earlier SLOOS-augmented read nudges the tone modestly more dovish:

- Activity: Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth with persistent softness in manufacturing and exports, aligning with the FOMC’s noting weak business fixed investment and exports.
- Labor/wages: Labor markets remained tight but wage growth was modest-to-moderate, with firms citing hiring constraints rather than overheating—consistent with muted inflation pressures.
- Prices: Price increases were described as modest, reinforcing sub-2% inflation and low inflation compensation in the FOMC statement.
- Credit: Anecdotes of tighter lending standards and cautious risk appetite, particularly around C&I and construction/land development, are consistent with SLOOS reports of tighter standards and weaker loan demand—adding a downside credit-channel risk.
- Policy implication: These Beige Book insights validate the case for a steady, accommodative stance and continued liquidity support (T-bill purchases/repo ops), while financial-stability considerations argue against aggressive easing.

Net: Slightly more dovish than the SLOOS-only update; raise the dovish score a bit.
